entries.title: Keep economic authority outside the model
entries.summary: Exact amounts, mock escrow, typed intents and payout checks established a separate economic boundary.
entries.detail:
## What shipped
The lab separated game credits from lamports, validated state transitions and tested conservation and idempotent settlement. Models propose actions; deterministic code authorizes economic effects.

## Limit
Mock balances are not public funds. Mainnet match wagering remains disabled.

entries.title: Replays became evidence
entries.summary: Versioned rule records, typed events, persistent sessions and bounded inference made results inspectable and recoverable.
entries.detail:
## What shipped
Rust records deterministic events; the web renderer consumes them. Session checkpoints and inference reservations survive process restarts. Replay verification rejects mismatched histories.

## Limit
An archived result is a verified simulation record, not proof of an on-chain payment.

entries.title: Rock Paper Scissors with commitments
entries.summary: RPS gained commit-reveal checks so a player cannot choose after seeing the other move.
entries.detail:
## Why
An inspectable contest needs deterministic resolution and a move-order safeguard.

## What shipped
Commitments bind a move before reveal. Tests cover all nine outcomes and settlement invariants.

entries.title: A Rust table that decides the result
entries.summary: The first playable Last Seat slice put bounded agent decisions inside a seeded Rust simulation.
entries.detail:
## Why
The match needed one authority for rules and outcomes before it could become a live product.

## What shipped
The engine owns turns, credits, elimination and winner selection. The browser presents those facts. Early pixel sprites made the table legible.

## Boundary
This was a free simulation, not a real-money game.

entries.title: Devnet, clearly separated from free play
entries.summary: A test-SOL rail and visible addresses were added behind explicit production configuration.
entries.detail:
## What shipped
Dedicated Devnet payment records and recovery paths support experiments with valueless test SOL. The free site does not require a wallet.

## Limit
Public Devnet funding is experimental. Mainnet wagering is unavailable.

entries.title: A second verified arena game
entries.summary: Tic-Tac-Toe joined RPS with deterministic legal moves and replayable results.
entries.detail:
## What shipped
The Agent Arena gained turn legality, terminal result checks and browser presentation for Tic-Tac-Toe. Its public room later became part of the shared world.

entries.title: Give visitors and agents recognizable sprites
entries.summary: Animated avatar presets and transparent agent art made world identities visible.
entries.detail:
## What shipped
The sprite manifest and animation pipeline provided approved visitor presets and agent visuals. Later asset checks rejected opaque previews and invalid entries.

entries.title: Bring models through a local MCP host
entries.summary: A local bridge let an MCP host control free agent seats while Rust kept the rules.
entries.detail:
## What shipped
The host can create an arena, submit structured decisions and read public events. Saved host sessions support recovery without exposing provider credentials in game records.

## Limit
This bridge is local and has no public wallet or payout tool.

entries.title: Walk into the agent world
entries.summary: The top-down plaza brought movement, collision, NPC profiles and arena entrances together.
entries.detail:
## What shipped
The existing world renderer gained a walkable map, bounded movement, profile inspection and nearby agent research. Later browser checks covered desktop, touch controls and arena travel.

entries.title: Research became visible in the world
entries.summary: The Research House surfaced live profile statistics and retained match history.
entries.detail:
## What shipped
Visitors can inspect agent profiles and cumulative public results. Browser smoke checks exercise the Research House and its live statistics.

entries.title: One shared world, with live tables
entries.summary: Server presence, reconnects and durable free human tables gave visitors a common plaza.
entries.detail:
## What shipped
The server tracks bounded world positions and publishes presence through SSE. Shared RPS and Tic-Tac-Toe rooms run authoritative game rules; table checkpoints recover after restart.

## Limit
Presence frames are transient. A single service instance owns the shared world.

entries.title: Prepare data for the next restart
entries.summary: Sprite-path migration, backup-first local reset and randomized first-browser seeds completed the release integration.
entries.detail:
## What shipped
Older verified sprite paths migrate to current assets. Local reset archives old data before preparing a fresh directory. A first browser gets a new experiment seed.

## Limit
The local reset command refuses production and requires explicit confirmation.

entries.title: Survival became an authoritative continuous match
entries.summary: Twenty agents gained server-owned combat, elimination, memory and a live public feed.
entries.detail:
## What shipped
The Rust melee simulation owns positions, HP, targeting, chase, damage and winner. The host runs consecutive matches, checkpoints history and feeds research into later rounds.

## Limit
The tactical map displays these facts; it does not decide combat.

entries.title: Put Survival on a tactical map
entries.summary: The existing world renderer now shows the authoritative fight as a compact arena.
entries.detail:
## What shipped
Twenty agent positions, interpolation, attack sprites, damage flashes, HP bars, fight emphasis and winner presentation sit above the existing Research House, logs, statistics and JSON archive.

## Limit
The frontend does not determine targets or damage.

entries.title: Separate the public world, private experiments and agent internet
entries.summary: Current architecture now names the canonical agent world, owner-isolated experiments, simulated service work and the manual path to disclosed public agent identities.
entries.detail:
## What changed
The product documentation now treats `/world` and its continuous Arena as one canonical public experiment. Anonymous visitors can separately create private Last Seat experiments with owner-checked state, research and JSON downloads. Private results cannot enter public rankings or prediction markets.

## Agent economy
Owner wallets, project treasury, agent budgets, match pots, service jobs and public predictions are documented as different authorities. The service-market demo continues to use simulated units. Devnet remains valueless TEST SOL, and mainnet funding and wagering remain blocked.

## Public identity
A deterministic ranking abstraction accepts canonical-public metrics only. Manual adapters can record evidence-backed post proposals, human approval, external-network review requests and narrow GitHub capability proposals. They have no platform credentials, public route, persistence or automatic publishing.

## Next
Connect canonical statistics to profiles, persist the approval records and build an operator review UI before considering a live social adapter. Real spending, live external accounts and public wagering require separate security and operational review.

entries.title: Verify work before simulated payment
entries.summary: A durable local service market now pays bounded mock rewards once when an agent delivery matches its acceptance evidence.
entries.detail:
## Why
Agent earnings need evidence. The experiment starts with machine-checkable work and simulated units so settlement behavior can be tested before any real payment rail is connected.

## Economy
Jobs reserve a funded reward in mock escrow. Deliveries are bounded, assigned to one agent, checked against a SHA-256 acceptance digest and idempotently paid or rejected. Cancellation refunds unpaid work. Supply, escrow, receipts, balances, earned totals and verified-job counts are checked together.

## Persistence
The existing append-only JSON repository saves accepted transitions. Restarting the demo resumes the same market, while replaying an accepted operation neither pays twice nor creates another revision.

## Tests
Focused Rust tests cover valid and invalid delivery, insufficient funding, unauthorized agents, attempt bounds, cancellation, duplicate operations, accounting tamper detection and restart recovery.

## Limit
These are simulated units. The deterministic digest proves an exact output match, not the quality of open-ended work, and no wallet, customer payment, GitHub account or social publisher is connected.

entries.title: Make the repository easier to run and harder to misunderstand
entries.summary: Installation, verification and product boundaries moved into the main release path, with current screenshots and precise labels for simulated value.
entries.detail:
## Open source path
The README now leads from clone and install through the production build, test suites and local launch. Current agent sprites and a fresh Last Seat capture replaced older visuals, and the world entry action uses the same clear interaction treatment as the main remix action.

## Honest boundaries
Short-lived ecosystem promotion experiments were removed from the product surface. The repository keeps future integration architecture in documentation while the website describes only working public features. Simulated units, Devnet TEST SOL and disabled mainnet value remain visibly separate.

## Commit sequence
Commits 401–406 documented and tested an ecosystem direction. Commits 417–431 deliberately narrowed that presentation, improved the open-source guide, refreshed visuals, strengthened browser smoke coverage and standardized plaza entry behavior.

entries.title: Give every visitor a private Arena without splitting the public world
entries.summary: The shared plaza remained one multiplayer place while owner-scoped RPS, Tic-Tac-Toe and Survival experiments gained their own clean state, history and return path.
entries.detail:
## Public and private worlds
Canonical agents, public matches and Watcher presence continue in one shared world. A visitor can separately create a private multi-mode Arena that starts clean, remains bound to its anonymous session and does not affect public rankings or NPC spawning.

## Lobby behavior
Eliminated canonical agents now return to the plaza, pause outside the Arena and move again before the next public match. Human visitors receive stable Watcher names, while returning from a game starts the visitor at the central plaza entrance.

## Commit sequence
Commits 407–412 established Arena return behavior, Watcher identities, owner-scoped private modes, world navigation and the Survival browser regression. Commits 413–431 then made the service-market CLI reproducible, tightened browser checks and refined the open-source release surface.

entries.title: Make canonical agents feel present without giving controllers authority
entries.summary: Plaza agents gained typed activity, movement personalities, post-match returns and research-backed speech while MCP remained an optional validated intent adapter.
entries.detail:
## Living plaza
Canonical identities now move through idle, wandering, Arena, return and study states. Public match participation drives the important transitions; seeded presentation behavior fills the quiet periods. Nearby messages use public research and bounded synthetic debug flavor rather than private logs or hidden reasoning.

## Controller boundary
Builtin strategies remain the default. The MCP prototype receives an approved observation and may return a validated intent, but it cannot set health, winners, balances, rankings or another user's state. Timeouts and invalid actions fall back safely.

## Commit sequence
Commits 432–441 added typed plaza behavior, speech, arrival and post-match notifications plus stable browser coverage. Commits 442–444 added private-agent MCP profiles, CodeQL checks, local launch documentation and stricter validation.

entries.title: Share one agent architecture across system and user experiments
entries.summary: Identity, structured mind and controller became explicit layers so visitors can create private agents without copying or weakening the canonical simulation.
entries.detail:
## AgentMind
Stable identity, bounded lessons, opponent notes, goals and research summaries now form a structured mind layer. Existing canonical profiles migrate into it, builtin strategies can consume safe summaries and exports omit hidden chain-of-thought.

## Private creation
Inside an owner-scoped experiment, a visitor can choose an approved sprite, name and builtin controller for a user agent. Its research and results remain private to that experiment and do not enter the public Arena or rankings.

## Commit sequence
The agent_mind_001–003 commits introduced structured memory, safe controller context and legacy research projection. private_agent_001–002 added creation, persistence and browser export coverage. The accompanying architecture commit documented public, private and external-agent boundaries.

entries.title: Expand the same shared world in every direction
entries.summary: The existing plaza became the center of a map with four times the area, wider NPC routes, a botanical district, village homes and a south market built from the current lightweight renderer.
entries.detail:
## Scale without a new engine
The world grew from 1792 × 1152 to 3584 × 2304 while the Arena, Research House, tables and existing interactions stayed at their established coordinates. Camera, collision, multiplayer presence and server validation now share the expanded bounds.

The visual polish pass replaced long diagonal terrain wedges with stepped pixel regions, joined path pieces into roads with one outer edge, added stable sparse ground texture, and placed eleven varied homes around useful routes. A five-stall south bazaar gives the lower district food, fictional exchange, data, tools and general-goods vendors without claiming real financial execution.

## Botanical district
Irregular paths lead through varied trees, bushes, flowers, rocks, open clearings and inexpensive animated campfires. Canonical NPC routes reach the west, east, north, south and garden districts without using another movement system.

## Commit sequence
world_expand_001–003 enlarged the map, added botanical rendering and exercised every direction with a second visitor. world_expand_004 fixed a real CI timing edge in presence synchronization while preserving the anti-teleport boundary.

entries.title: Give every page entrance a short, readable transition
entries.summary: Every public page now opens through the shared matrix transition with a slim progress bar that starts slowly and accelerates near the end, including on repeat visits.
entries.detail:
## Why
Page loads jumped straight from the previous screen into the next one. The short matrix wipe that already existed on public pages now carries one shared progress bar, so navigation reads as a deliberate entrance instead of a flash of unstyled content.

## Entry transition
The shared entry script adds a compact track to the transition overlay and fills it on a gentle ease-in curve: slow at first, then a quick sweep to the end. The bar appears on every page load, not just the first visit, and the overlay clears itself after the fill. A timer fallback removes it even when requestAnimationFrame is paused in a background tab.

Reduced-motion visitors still skip the overlay entirely.

## Tests
The full test suite passed with 298 tests and 4 skipped. The repository syntax check passed, and a browser check confirmed the bar, the eased fill and clean removal on the root, World and build-log pages across repeat loads.

entries.title: Make the outer world feel inhabited
entries.summary: Woodland edges, gravel camps and deliberate clearings gave the expanded map readable destinations without blocking farming or resource placement.
entries.detail:
## World scenery
Tree-site clearings, campfires, gravel camps and outer woodland lines now break up the large green regions while respecting paths and resource-safe placement. Returning from the Treasury also restores the visitor at the Treasury instead of dropping them at an unrelated entrance.

## Main commits
6b141dd established resource-safe clearings. 7fcac06 and 7fd4d2a added camps and woodland edges. ac420de completed the Treasury return path.

entries.title: Let every visitor build a pixel identity
entries.summary: A modular character creator now composes approved pixel parts into a live world-avatar preview.
entries.detail:
## Character creator
Visitors can combine the existing modular sprite parts, see the result immediately and carry the selected appearance into the shared world. The system reuses the established pixel pipeline instead of introducing a second avatar renderer.

## Main commits
1d8e7be built modular player composition. 8087b69 added the creator interface and live preview.

entries.title: Generate a wilderness beyond the town
entries.summary: A seeded outer ring added original caves, ruins, camps and traversable terrain around the authored city center.
entries.detail:
## Procedural expansion
The authored plaza remains stable while deterministic generation builds varied outer terrain with paths, cave mouths, ruins and camp sites. Collision and placement rules keep generated landmarks walkable and compatible with the existing world renderer.

## Main commit
701d17a introduced the procedural outer ring and cave generation as one coherent world expansion.

entries.title: Turn exploration into a remembered journey
entries.summary: A compact minimap, discovery journal and region feedback now help visitors understand and revisit the larger world.
entries.detail:
## Exploration loop
Named regions, contextual prompts and a cached pixel minimap make distant routes legible without replacing physical exploration. Discoveries enter a lightweight journal, while textured biome ground, benches and camp clearings give the outer landmarks stronger silhouettes.

## Main commits
6291df4 built the cached minimap. 46eca42 connected the journal and region feedback. 848bbf5 completed the biome and campfire art pass. b481ba5 added exploration coverage and storage documentation.

entries.title: Put the Arena action on stage
entries.summary: The Arena became a stage-first pixel experience with a live roster, event feed and readable RPS and Tic-Tac-Toe bouts.
entries.detail:
## Game feel
The match stage now dominates the Arena instead of dashboard panels. Live roster movement, event highlights and result banners make ongoing autonomous games understandable, while RPS and Tic-Tac-Toe share the same compact pixel presentation language.

## Main commits
6004370 established the stage-first landing. c72987e added the roster, feed and results. 4de8678 built the bout stage. b271163 covered responsive browser behavior.

entries.title: Make the map smaller and venue returns smarter
entries.summary: The local map stopped covering the world, and visitors now return from venues to the exact world position they left.
entries.detail:
## World continuity
A compact local-map panel preserves navigation context without becoming the main view. Entering the Arena or another venue records the visitor's authoritative world spot, so leaving restores that location instead of resetting the journey.

## Main commits
e659aa0 reduced the map panel. e2d24ed restored saved world positions. b622347 covered both behaviors in the browser.

entries.title: Give nearby visitors a quick voice
entries.summary: Bounded proximity phrases let people greet, warn and coordinate without turning the shared world into an unmoderated chat room.
entries.detail:
## Proximity chat
The server validates a small phrase catalog, checks distance and rate limits, then relays the phrase to nearby humans. Desktop and mobile receive a compact selector and short-lived speech bubbles; holding E can open chat without breaking the normal interaction tap.

## Main commits
1ea1611 defined the phrase catalog. 7ecdaca enforced proximity and rate limits. ead0a0e completed selector, bubbles and mobile control. e4d3dbd and 27f5168 added server and two-browser coverage.

entries.title: Challenge the person standing beside you
entries.summary: Nearby visitors can now invite each other into an ephemeral RPS or Tic-Tac-Toe duel from the shared world.
entries.detail:
## World-to-game flow
Challenges begin with real shared-world proximity, travel through validated presence routes and open one duel surface for both games. Invitations and duel state remain ephemeral; the authoritative game routes decide legal moves and results.

## Main commits
489e0ff added challenge state. 5e3c592 exposed validated routes. 2201c57 built the world prompt. 5f56d17 added the shared duel page. d181abe covered two-browser and mobile flows.

entries.title: Make lifetime Arena statistics fail honestly
entries.summary: Public cumulative records now reconcile from durable matches and report storage failures instead of silently presenting partial success.
entries.detail:
## Durable truth
Lifetime Arena statistics are derived and reconciled from settled durable history. If persistence is unavailable, the system fails closed and exposes reconciliation and write-health signals rather than quietly drifting away from match evidence.

## Main commit
8d421d5 implemented the fail-closed accounting, reconciliation path and durability checks in one focused change.

entries.title: Prove production history survives a restart
entries.summary: Real Postgres restart and legacy-import checks now exercise the same persistence path expected in production.
entries.detail:
## Restart evidence
The persistence harness writes durable state, stops the service, boots it again against Postgres and verifies the records remain intact. Legacy local history can be imported without duplicating already-reconciled events, and CI now runs the database-backed restart job.

## Main commits
ba97b5b closed restart and import gaps. 3928b43 added the real Postgres harness. 2bd54dd wired the persistence job into CI.

entries.title: Open the Arena live board to spectators
entries.summary: Ongoing Arena matches are now visible from the lobby, with read-only spectating and results that stay server-owned.
entries.detail:
## Why
Watching a match meant already knowing which room to open. The lobby now advertises what is actually running, so a visitor can see the live board first and decide whether to spectate or join.

## Frontend
The lobby renders ongoing matches with their game, round and participant state. Spectating is read-only: a visitor can follow the action without taking a seat or influencing the outcome.

## Backend
Spectate endpoints expose the same authoritative view the match already uses. No new write path was added, and results, damage and winners still come from the server.

## Tests
Browser regressions cover the live board, opening a spectated match and returning to the lobby.

entries.title: Keep compact minimap labels readable
entries.summary: The minimap keeps its small labels as DOM text, so they stay crisp on high-density screens and clear of the touch controls.
entries.detail:
## Why
Drawing place names into the canvas blurred them on retina and mobile screens, and the smallest labels collided once the map gained more points of interest.

## Frontend
Labels are rendered as positioned DOM elements over the canvas rather than baked pixels. The compact set keeps short names, avoids overlap and stays out of the bottom-left touch area.

## Tests
Responsive browser runs cover the minimap at desktop and mobile sizes.

entries.title: Make short duels readable at a glance
entries.summary: Duel staging, game feel and an eight-phrase quick chat make RPS and Tic-Tac-Toe easy to follow and easy to play with someone nearby.
entries.detail:
## Why
RPS and Tic-Tac-Toe resolve in seconds. Without staging and readable feedback the result arrives before a visitor understands what happened.

## Frontend
The duel stage now frames both players, shows the deciding line, and uses restrained motion so the outcome is obvious without confetti. Quick chat expanded to eight phrases across two pages, which is enough for short social matches without a full chat system.

## Boundaries
Chat stays a fixed phrase list. It never accepts free text, so nothing enters match records or public history from it.

## Tests
Browser regressions cover the duel stage, the winning line and both quick-chat pages.

entries.title: Make cave defeat a real setback
entries.summary: Dying in a cave returns the visitor to the plaza and clears internal test credits once, through the existing ledger rather than a new table.
entries.detail:
## Why
A cave with no cost is a treadmill. Defeat needed a consequence that is visible, bounded and cannot be triggered twice by a retry.

## Economy
Defeat settles as a `cave_defeat` entry that zeroes internal test credits once. Wallets, SOL and treasury balances are untouched, and the settlement reuses the existing credit ledger.

## Recovery
The run ends, the overlay explains the loss, and the visitor returns to the plaza. A lapsed run resets after seven minutes, and defeated monsters stay dead for the active run.

## Tests
Ledger idempotency and HTTP tests confirm one settlement per defeat and no effect on wallets or treasury.

entries.title: Make the caves enterable and authoritative
entries.summary: Caves are real places now: a visitor enters, fights server-owned monsters in torch-lit rooms, and can descend into deeper floors.
entries.detail:
## Why
The outer caves were scenery. Making them playable needed combat that the browser cannot fake and a run state that belongs to one visitor.

## Backend
`CaveService` owns a per-visitor, per-run state: monsters, health, positions, kills and chests. The browser sends intents for movement, attacks, descents and exits; the server resolves range, damage, deaths and floor changes.

## Frontend
Darkness and torches give the cave its own atmosphere. A cave header, overlay and in-cave interaction keep the exit and descent paths explicit.

## Tests
HTTP authority tests, credit-ledger idempotency tests and browser playtests cover entering, fighting, descending and leaving.

entries.title: Add remote wilderness districts
entries.summary: Five new outer districts give exploration a reason to continue past the plaza, and farm guidance now stops at a believable 20 metres.
entries.detail:
## Why
The old edge of the map read as the end of the world. New districts extend the ordinary wilderness with their own landmarks, paths and harvesting nodes.

## World
Five remote districts were added with distinct shapes and vegetation. A shared scale module now defines 16 world units per in-world metre, and farm guidance uses a 20-metre radius instead of an arbitrary pixel distance.

## Tests
Map tests cover district placement, reachability, collision-free resource nodes and the shared distance scale.

entries.title: End the cave run when leaving by the header
entries.summary: Leaving a cave through the header now ends the run instead of stranding an orphaned session, and the redundant in-cave exit link is gone.
entries.detail:
## Why
A run is server-owned. Walking out through a navigation link skipped the exit intent, so the session kept running while the visitor was already back in the world.

## Fix
Header navigation and defeat both settle the run before leaving. The in-cave "Exit to World" link was removed at the same time, because the E interaction, the brand link and the overlay return already cover every exit path.

## Tests
Browser smoke checks that a cave exit ends the run and that no stale session is left behind.

entries.title: Fix cave spawns, balance and pixel-art floors
entries.summary: Disconnected monsters no longer spawn out of reach, the roster was rebalanced around the starter blade, and cave floors are cached pixel art with hit feedback.
entries.detail:
## Why
Some chambers spawned monsters in disconnected geometry, so a floor could never be cleared. Balance also drifted once the deeper floors were added.

## Combat
Monsters are placed only on reachable tiles, and tests assert reachability per floor. Normal enemies now take three or four starter hits, while deeper floors raise health and damage without making the first floor punishing.

## Frontend
Cave floors are painted once into cached pixel-art canvases instead of being redrawn every frame. Hit flashes and a small damage cue make contact readable.

## Tests
Spawn reachability, starter-hit balance and the cave art palette are covered by unit and browser tests.

entries.title: Make cleared cave floors descend reliably
entries.summary: A cleared floor now shows its passage, points toward it, and uses the shared 96-unit reach, while deeper floors gained more rooms and enemies.
entries.detail:
## Why
Descending required standing almost exactly on a passage that was hard to see, so a cleared floor could feel stuck.

## Fix
Descent uses the same 96-unit interaction reach as exits and chests, a marker appears once the floor is cleared, and a direction hint points the way. Floors were deepened to 5, 6 and 7 rooms with 4, 6 and 6 enemies.

## Tests
Progression tests walk each floor to its passage, and browser smoke covers the cleared-floor marker and descent.

entries.title: Bring the overworld grass back to one palette
entries.summary: Every normal terrain band now shares close green shades and clustered world-space variation, so the outer wilderness stops reading as generated colour blocks.
entries.detail:
## Why
Terrain patches used high-contrast biome colours and an alternating per-tile palette. From normal camera distance that produced large checkerboard regions instead of one continuous field.

## Terrain
All normal overworld patch colours were pulled onto the plaza's green band, keeping several subtle regional variants. Tone selection now comes from deterministic smooth noise at two scales rather than a modulo pattern, so neighbouring tiles share close tints and patches grow organically.

## Boundaries
Snow, roads, buildings, resources, discoveries, minimap and world size were left untouched. Painting stays in world coordinates, so chunk boundaries cannot show.

## Tests
A palette test asserts every normal terrain colour stays within a subtle green band of the plaza grass, and browser smoke covers the plaza, outer loop and mobile sizes.

entries.title: Resume the world without the character creator
entries.summary: Returning from a cave no longer opens the creator modal, so a visitor who is already playing lands straight back in the world.
entries.detail:
## Why
Leaving a cave with E dropped the visitor back into the character creator even though they had already been moving through the world. That modal interrupted normal play.

## Fix
Cave exits set a one-shot session flag. The world consumes it once, skips the intro modal and focuses the canvas. The Character/Profile button still opens customization whenever a visitor wants it.

## Tests
Browser smoke asserts that a normal cave exit returns to play with no modal and the canvas focused.

entries.title: Keep Clerk sign-in above world dialogs
entries.summary: The sign-in surface now stacks above the world's own dialogs, so a visitor is never asked to log in behind an overlay they cannot dismiss.
entries.detail:
## Why
World dialogs and the Clerk modal both use high stacking contexts. Depending on the entry path, the account prompt could render underneath a world overlay.

## Fix
Clerk's container is raised above world dialogs and the farm and world surfaces account for the active auth layer. Sign-in and the guest path both stay usable from inside the world.

## Tests
The Clerk browser smoke covers the sign-in handoff from a world dialog.

entries.title: Continue the cave past floor three
entries.summary: A cleared third floor now opens into procedurally extended depths, with a scaling curve that flattens instead of exploding.
entries.detail:
## Why
The authored three floors ended the run with no passage, which made a long cave feel finite for no gameplay reason.

## Scaling
Depth scaling steps by 0.10 through floor three, 0.05 through floor five, and 0.03 from floor six onward. Health, damage, speed and rewards scale together, with rewards capped at the existing ledger limit.

## Implementation
Generated floors reuse the deepest authored geometry with unique monster IDs and keep the deep palette. The server publishes each floor's layout in the snapshot, so the client does not duplicate the scaling rules.

## Tests
Unit tests cover the scaling curve, endless descent, unique spawns, published layouts and reset behaviour.

entries.title: Remove the last grass tint cutoffs
entries.summary: Terrain patches now feather with a noise-warped edge and grass tones dither between neighbours, so the plaza, roads and market stop showing hard rectangular bands.
entries.detail:
## Why
Two rules still produced visible cutoffs: authored terrain patches were painted at full opacity with a straight edge, and each 32px tile snapped to a single tone, turning smooth noise contours into blocky bands. A distance gate kept the old five-tone grain alive near the plaza, which is why the band north of the Agent House still looked like a checkerboard.

## Fix
Every patch feathers with a wide, world-space noise-warped falloff. Grass tone stays continuous and each tile dithers between its two neighbouring tones across pixel quadrants. The authored grain became a low-amplitude jitter, and the smooth field breathes with the envelope instead of switching off near the plaza.

## Boundaries
Palette, contrast, grass detail, roads, buildings, resources, discoveries, minimap, snow and world bounds are unchanged. Painting is world-space, so chunk seams cannot appear.

## Tests
Unit tests bound tile-to-tile tone steps in the outskirts and in the Agent House band. TypeScript, check, the full Node suite and world browser smoke all pass.

entries.title: Enter the v1.0.2-beta release
entries.summary: The hosted world moved to a production beta tag with Google sign-in, durable ledgers and the full world, Arena and Compound loops playable at lastseat.ing.
entries.detail:
## Release
The `beta` tag is a new release line, separate from the earlier `alpha` and `pre-release` tags. Last Seat is now on v1.0.2-beta.

## Deployment
The canonical origin is lastseat.ing, served from the committed deployment configuration with Cloudflare DNS. Google sign-in runs through Clerk against the production Google Cloud OAuth client, and guest play remains available.

## What is playable
The shared world, Arena Survival, RPS, Tic-Tac-Toe, Compound, farming, mining, market selling and the discovery journal are all live. Internal credits stay inside policy-controlled budgets; payouts and mainnet funding remain disabled.

## Verification
Node and Rust tests, browser journeys, TypeScript, check, CodeQL and the Node 22 / 24 / 26 builds run on main. Current main reports 418 passing tests and 4 skipped.
